newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia's Pennu says 1996 sales rose 85 pct.
newsitem.headline: Estonia's Pennu says 1996 sales rose 85 pct.

text.p: Estonian computer company Pennu, listed on the stock market, said on Thursday that net sales in 1996 grew by 85 percent to 121.2 million kroons from 65.6 million kroons.
It said in a statement that export net sales rose to 11.2 million kroons from 900,000 kroons.
The company earlier announced a 3.5 million kroon profit forecast for the first half of 1997 and said it would be seeking to increase sales in neighbouring countries this year.
The company expects to release its 1996 audited balance sheet in late February.
Pennu last year launched an international and local stock offering worth 6.8 million kroons.
Institutional investors from the U.S., U.K. and Scandinavia took part in the international offer.
Pennu is Estonia's second largest computer firm and assembles imported hardware to sell under its own name.
It also last year agreed to build with Western Digital a hard disk repair centre in Estonia to service eastern Europe.
